status_note: First-authored 10-week overhead-mobility arc — the shoulder / thoracic / scap coordination needed to snatch, OHS, and press without impingement. Evidence base drawn from whitepaper 04_handstand_walk.md and motor-learning literature (whitepaper 03), plus 4 shoulder-specific citations that need pre-launch URL verification.

goals.primary: Add ROM-under-load overhead — shoulder flexion, thoracic extension, scap upward rotation
goals.secondary: Reduce anterior-shoulder irritation risk during heavy overhead work (snatch, OHS, press)
explicit_non_goals: Building a snatch PR — mobility opens the door; technique + strength walks through it
Replacing a physio evaluation for actual shoulder pathology

principles.rule: Passive ROM before active ROM before loaded ROM.
principles.detail: Ludewig & Cook 2000 documented that impingement risk rises when scap upward rotation lags shoulder flexion under load. We build the kinematic pattern before we add weight.

principles.rule: Every drill card ships a Wulf-compliant external-focus cue.
principles.detail: Wulf 1998, 2013 — external focus outperforms internal for skill retention. `reach for the ceiling` beats `contract your lats`.

principles.rule: Scap upward-rotation drills come before shoulder-flexion drills in every session.
principles.detail: Ludewig & Reynolds 2009 — scap dyskinesis (upper-trap dominance) is the most consistently documented kinematic association with symptomatic impingement in athletes. Fix the sequence, not just the range.

principles.rule: No bouncing / rebound stretches at end-range shoulder flexion.
principles.detail: Reinold 2007 — active rotator-cuff engagement should precede end-range positioning. Ballistic end-range invites impingement.
Karni 1998, Walker 2003 consolidation — motor patterns consolidate with sleep between sessions. Short daily > long infrequent for mobility acquisition.

plan_tiers.label: Foundation — Wall-arm-raise fails / can't reach vertical
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 10: supine shoulder flexion 165-175°, empty-bar OHS to parallel without heel lift, first snatch-grip Sotts press.

plan_tiers.label: Progression — Vertical passive, loaded overhead is stiff
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 10: 180° passive + loaded OHS at 50% BW to parallel, snatch-grip Sotts at bar weight for reps.

plan_tiers.label: Push — Vertical loaded, chasing efficiency + endurance
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: Overhead endurance (Turkish get-up hold ≥ 30s each side at 24kg), snatch balance to 60% snatch 1RM without sequencing errors.

questions.label: Realistically, how many days per week can you commit?
questions.help: Honest answer wins. If your ceiling is 2, we'll tell you upfront whether this program can deliver on its claim at that dose.

physical_tests.label: Supine shoulder flexion
physical_tests.instructions: Lie flat on your back, arms overhead. Have someone measure the angle between your upper arm and the floor. 180 = elbows touching floor. Ballpark is fine.

physical_tests.label: OHS depth (hip below knee)
physical_tests.instructions: Empty-bar overhead squat to the lowest position you can hold without heel lift or forward collapse. Measure how far your hip crease is BELOW the top of the knee. Positive = hip below knee. Zero = parallel.

physical_tests.label: Turkish get-up overhead hold
physical_tests.instructions: Get-up to the tall-sit or half-kneeling position with a KB (choose a challenging but controllable weight). Hold overhead. Time until arm buckles or drifts out of vertical.

safety_gates.block_body: A diagnosed rotator-cuff tear needs a rehab pathway, not a mobility program. Return once cleared for overhead loading.
Recent dislocation requires clinician clearance and typically capsule-stability work before overhead ROM work is safe.
Cervical radicular symptoms need their own workup. Overhead ROM work can amplify a nerve-root irritation.

phases.name: Kinematic base · Weeks 1–3
phases.goal: Build passive ROM + scap sequencing before we add load.
phases.rationale: Ludewig 2000/2009 — impingement is scap dyskinesis + upward-rotation lag, not raw shoulder joint tightness. Base = fix the sequence.

phases.name: Active + light-loaded · Weeks 4–7
phases.goal: Add active ROM + light loaded overhead. Sotts press, TGU, empty bar OHS.
phases.rationale: Reinold 2007 — rotator-cuff activation precedes end-range loading. Adding load builds the pattern under stress without impingement.

phases.name: Load + retest · Weeks 8–10
phases.goal: Consolidate loaded ROM. Retest at week 10.
phases.rationale: Karni 1998, Walker 2003 — consolidation with daily short sessions. Retest via shoulder-flexion goniometer + empty-bar OHS depth.

blocks.name: Thoracic prep · daily
blocks.note: Wall slides, foam-roller extensions, KB arm-bar. Prepares scap-thoracic mobility before shoulder work.

blocks.name: Scap activation
blocks.note: Band pull-apart variants, prone Y/T/W. Wake up lower trap + serratus so upward rotation happens before elevation.

blocks.name: Passive shoulder flexion
blocks.note: PVC pass-throughs, supine Sotts hold with light weight, wall-facing arm raises. Rib cage stays down.

blocks.name: Active shoulder flexion
blocks.note: Wall walks (from Handstand Walk drill library), face-away wall slides, half-kneeling reach. Active rotator-cuff engagement required.

blocks.name: Loaded overhead
blocks.note: Snatch-grip Sotts press · KB bottoms-up press · Turkish get-up. Load stays sub-maximal; ROM is the metric, not the number.

blocks.name: Overhead endurance
blocks.note: TGU hold (30s each side, working up), overhead KB carry, snatch balance.

blocks.name: Daily reset · pre-bed
blocks.note: 3 min of thoracic + shoulder pass-throughs at bedtime. Grease the pattern; sleep does the consolidation (Walker 2003).

weekly_template.note: Multi-dimensional generation. Each block declares a capability_slot; composeSlotDrills fills items[] from drill_library at the user's estimated level, attaching an external-focus cue (Wulf & Shea 2002). Contextual interference applies from Week 3+ (Shea & Morgan 1979 · Wulf & Shea 2002).

retest_metrics.display_name: Overhead squat depth (hip crease vs top of knee)
Turkish get-up hold time (best of L / R)

immediate_actions.action: Measure supine shoulder flexion — record baseline
Wall-slide test video (optional) — watch for scap dyskinesis pattern

physiological_targets.confidence: realistic for Foundation and Progression; stretch for Push (structural ROM limits)

push.confidence: fair — structural ROM begins to dominate near 190°

session_rationale.why_scap_first: Ludewig & Cook 2000, Ludewig & Reynolds 2009 — scap upward-rotation timing is the dominant driver of subacromial space. Fix sequence before adding load.
session_rationale.why_daily_short: Karni 1998, Walker 2003 consolidation — motor patterns require inter-session sleep for stabilisation. 10 min daily > 45 min biweekly.
session_rationale.why_load_early: Reinold 2007 catalogued rotator-cuff EMG activation across a wide range of common drills; many light-load and banded variants produced cuff activation greater than typical bodyweight drills at comparable positions. Light load in Phase 2 leverages that catalogue to bias cuff engagement earlier. This is an engineering read of an EMG review, not an RCT of light-load vs bodyweight for shoulder-mobility outcome — see engineering_choices_flagged.
session_rationale.why_external_focus_cues: Wulf 1998, 2013 — external-focus cues (reach the ceiling) outperform internal (contract your lats) for motor retention.

engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: No RCT specifies the exact duration for shoulder-mobility work in athletes. Karni/Walker consolidation lit supports weekly re-testing over several weeks; 10 weeks is engineering.

engineering_choices_flagged.choice: Sotts press as primary loaded-overhead drill
engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: Coaching consensus in the weightlifting community. Not RCT'd against alternatives (KB press variants) for shoulder-mobility outcome specifically.
Historical / anecdotal (Pavel Tsatsouline lineage). Reproducible + measurable, but not RCT-validated as a shoulder-mobility outcome. We use it as a proxy for overhead endurance.
Widely used in weightlifting warm-ups; no dedicated RCT.

engineering_choices_flagged.choice: Supine flexion goniometer as primary retest
engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: Kim 2013 documented supine flexion reliability; whether supine translates to loaded overhead is engineering inference — hence retest_metrics includes both supine AND OHS depth.

engineering_choices_flagged.choice: Light external load in Phase 2 to bias cuff activation early
engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: Reinold 2007 is a cross-drill EMG catalogue, not an RCT of light-load vs bodyweight for shoulder-mobility outcome. We treat the earlier-load bias as an engineering read of that catalogue.

contraindications: Diagnosed rotator-cuff tear (partial or full) — needs physio pathway
Recent shoulder dislocation / subluxation — capsule stability first
Cervical radicular symptoms into the arm — needs workup
Adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder) — separate rehab protocol
Active AC-joint irritation — end-range flexion can amplify
adaptive_engine_hooks: day_adjustment on symptom 'shoulder pain during flexion' → drop loaded_overhead this session; scap + thoracic only
amber week (≥3 amber shoulder symptom days) → skip loaded_overhead for a full week
phase_end evaluator: retest goniometer + OHS depth → tier promotion if targets hit

onboarding_steps.title: What Terav will and won't do here
onboarding_steps.body_md: Overhead Mobility is a supplement, not a shoulder rehab. If you have a diagnosed labrum, cuff, or biceps injury, work with a physio first. Terav sharpens a range you already have — it does not restore range you've lost to pathology.
